templates.scene: Empty office cubicle. Two Office coworkers (Stanley in a leather jacket, Oscar in a white shirt) do a stiff, half-hearted dance in front of the desk.
templates.slot: How [your back / your body / your spine] expects you to [move or react] after [an everyday back-pain moment]. The stiff, reluctant dance is the punchline.

templates.scene: Grocery store aisle. Beaker from The Muppets in a floral shirt slowly grows, wide-eyed and alarmed, like he just got caught.
templates.slot: When you [do something awkward because of back pain, in public] and [someone sees you]. Beaker's caught-in-the-act panic is the punchline.
templates.description: Grocery photo, the caught-in-the-aisle reaction, the sound from that format.

templates.scene: Exam room, a doctor in a white coat waits by an empty table. Carlton from Fresh Prince does his full Carlton dance next to him.
templates.slot: Doctor: [asks what you were doing / how it happened]? then a last line 'Me at [a fun event or moment where you overdid it]:'. Carlton's big dance is what you were doing.

templates.scene: Exam room, a doctor in a white coat waits by an empty table. Kermit the Frog flails his arms and legs in a floppy, uncoordinated dance.
templates.slot: Doctor: [asks you to show or do a movement, stretch, or routine] then a last line 'Me:'. Kermit's flailing is your attempt.

templates.scene: Cozy living room. Two cats stand on their back legs side by side and dance in sync.
